problem: Which expression gives the vertical asymptotes of the function $f(x)=2\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{4}-{60}^{∘}),$ where $x$ is measured in degrees? Assume that $n$ is an integer.

feedback.problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the vertical asymptotes of the function $f(x)=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{3})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
feedback.worked_solution:
The asymptotes of $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x$ coincide with the zeros of $y=\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ and are given by the following expression

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the asymptotes of $\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{3}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{3}).$ This gives

$$
\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{3}=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{3} & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ \frac{x}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi -\frac{\pi }{3} \\ \frac{x}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{2\cdot \pi }{6}+2n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{3}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the expression giving all the vertical asymptotes is $x=\frac{\pi }{3}+2n\pi ,$ where $n$ is an integer.
